title: add-jsonschema-strict-mode-validation-openai-compat-and-better-error-messages
author: Jordan Kim
description: Adds strict JSON Schema response_format support with runtime validation, improved error reporting, and an OpenAI-compatibility layer for schema errors. Motivation: customers need deterministic structured outputs for downstream parsing and stronger guarantees when using response_format/schema in production. This PR implements a runtime validation pass that runs after decoding (configurable: strict|warn|off), surfaces precise error messages with path and schema rule failures, and provides a compact OpenAI-compatible error payload for clients that expect the classic OpenAI error shape. Changes include server-side validator, SDK client helper updates, new unit and integration tests, and docs/examples. Checklist: - [x] design review (ENG-1428) - [x] implement validator and strict-mode path - [x] add OpenAI-compatible error mapping - [x] update Python/TS SDK helpers and examples - [x] add unit/integration tests and CI - [x] update docs and release notes Notes: strict mode will reject responses that do not match the schema and return a 400 with structured error metadata; warn mode will accept the response but record a QA metric and attach the validation result in the response metadata. See migration_instructions and release_notes fields for developer guidance.

release_notes: Structured output: add response_format=json_schema with strict/warn/off validation modes; OpenAI-compatible error payload for validation failures; SDK helpers to surface validation results; performance notes and metric recommendations.
merge_commit_summary: squash: add jsonschema strict-mode validation and OpenAI-compatible error mapping
tests_summary: Added ~30 unit tests across python/ts for validator behavior and 3 integration tests exercising strict/warn/off; CI flaky test stabilized.
notes_on_backward_compatibility: Default is warn for hosted tier to preserve existing behavior. Users on Dedicated/Private can opt into strict mode. SDK helpers maintain backward-compatible APIs; error payloads when strict mode rejects will be a 400 with new validation metadata but old clients will still receive a 400 code as before.
error_messages_examples: {"message": "Response did not match JSON Schema: /top_level_field - missing required property 'user_id'", "code": "validation_error", "severity": "error"}
{"message": "Type mismatch at /items/0/amount: expected number but got string", "code": "validation_error", "path": "/items/0/amount"}
{"message": "OpenAI-compatible: validation failed for response_format schema", "type": "invalid_request_error", "errors": [{"message": "missing required property 'user_id'", "path": "/user_id"}] }
migration_instructions: - Hosted customers: no immediate action; default remains warn. - To enable strict validation, set response_format.strict_mode=\"strict\" in the request or configure at route level. - For SDK users, call validate_response(schema, mode) helper to pre-flight local checks. - If you see 400 with validation errors, use the provided 'errors' array in the payload to repair prompts or adjust schema.
